To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a transition from rolls (or squares or rhombuses) to hexagons is possible in reaction diffusion systems and the transition is hysteretic.
we have shown that the transition from rolls to the hexagonal pattern in a reaction-diffusion system (the Gierer-Meinhard model) can be induced by varying the intrinsic length scales of the system.
the intrinsic length scales of reaction diffusion systems are varied by quasi-staticly changing the diffusion constant and that the system shows transition from roll pattern to hexagonal one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transition from one pattern to another under the variation of a system’s intrinsic length scales.
the effect of intrinsic length scales on the pattern formation of a reaction diffusion model.
the effect of intrinsic length scale on pattern selection in reaction diffusion systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intrinsic length scales of the reaction diffusion system can be varied in the quasi-static way, which is the main point of this paper, by changing the diffusion constant.
the transition from rolls to a hexagonal pattern under variation of the intrinsic length scales is possible and that it is hysteretic or of first order.
the system undergoes a transition from rolls (w=1) to hexagons (w=3) under the variation of the diffusion constant of activator, and the transition is hysteretic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intrinsic length scales of the system can play the role of control parameter in the transition of pattern.
the intrinsic length scales of the system can be varied by changing the diffusion constant and a transition between rolls and hexagons can be detected under such variation.
the intrinsic length scales of the system play an important role in pattern formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transition to hexagonal pattern is possible even in a reaction diffusion system where the diffusion constant of activator is larger than the inhibitor.
such transitions can be induced in the reaction-diffusion systems by varying the intrinsic length scales.
the intrinsic length scale of the system plays an important role in deciding its pattern.
